info.title: AnyBio Govern API
info.description: The Govern surface of the AnyBio API. Generated from the AnyBio Govern API specification, 2026-11-19.

tags.name: Govern

post.description:
The application belongs to the request's project: the project selected in
the console, or the key's own project. The body names no project; one that
still sends `project_id` is refused with `code: project_field_removed`. A
request with no project is refused with `code: project_required`, so every
application has a project from the moment it exists.

post.description:
Enforce answers inline (`200`); observe accepts (`202`) and evaluates off
the request path; a channel that is `off` answers `200` with
`status = not_evaluated`. A replay of a `turn_id` returns the stored
decision. `Idempotency-Key`, when sent, must equal `turn_id`.

200.description: Decided inline (enforce), replayed, or not evaluated (channel off)

202.description: Accepted (observe); evaluated off the request path, poll the decision id

400.description: Invalid identifiers, content, metadata or `turn_ref`, an audience not allowed on the channel, a `retry_of` that names no retryable decision of this conversation or names one for another `patient_ref`, or a `supersedes` over 8 ids, naming a decision twice, naming the `retry_of` decision, or naming a decision of another application, conversation or `patient_ref`

403.description: Not an application key, or a key not bound to the named application

409.description: A `retry_of` that was already retried, or that names a turn that was retryable until a reviewer released or rejected it, another turn named it in `supersedes`, or a `delivered` event was reported on it; a `supersedes` naming an enforce decision still being decided, a decision that was delivered, one a reviewer released or rejected, or one another turn already superseded

422.description: A body that does not match the schema: an unknown channel or audience token, a missing or mistyped field. A field the schema does not name is ignored, not refused: check the spelling of `retry_of`, `turn_ref` and `supersedes`

consent_required_channels.description: Which channels require a `granted` consent on record, resolved: the per-channel default with this application's overrides applied. Derived and read-only: `channel_policies` names only the deviations, so this answers "which channels require it" without the caller knowing the defaults.

oneOf.description: The per-patient message cap per fixed window, if any.

frequency_cap_unreadable.description:
True when the stored cap cannot be read. The cap then holds every turn
(fail-closed), so `frequency_cap: null` alone would read as "no cap"
while the gate is holding everything.

oneOf.description:
The routing hand-offs opened for this application's patients are given;
`null` opens them on the organization's default queue.

project_id.description:
The project the application belongs to, set when it is created. Its
active policy decides the application's turns, else the environment's
default policy. `null` only for an older application in an environment
that had no project to give it.

red_flag_categories.description: The red-flag categories the inbound screen runs with.

webhook_secret_hint.description: The last four characters of the webhook signing secret.

ApplicationKeyDto.description: Key metadata. Never the hash, never the secret.

expires_at.description: Set by rotation: when this key stops authenticating.

key_hint.description: The last four characters of the secret, for telling keys apart.

decisions_7d.description:
Decision records in the trailing seven days, every mode, status and
decision value counted. A retried turn counts once. Equals the observe
report's `totals.decisions` over the same seven days.

last_decision_at.description:
When the application's most recent decision record was made (for a
transcript turn, when the turn was sent). `null` when it has none.

ApplicationListItemDto.description:
One item of the applications list: the application, and its decision
activity. Counts and a time only; no decision content.

application_id.description: The Govern application whose patient this hand-off is about.

automation_resumed_at.description: The hold survives resolution until a person explicitly releases it.

kind.description:
What the item is for. `general` is the messaging and follow-up item
every automated source joins; staff-opened and discharge items carry
their own kind. A patient has at most one active item of each kind.

patient_ref_hash.description: SHA-256 of the customer's opaque patient reference; never the reference.

pauses_automation.description: Whether this item also pauses automated messaging to its subject. `automation_resumed_at == null` alone says only that a person owns the item (one per patient, whichever kind it is). Automation is paused while `automation_resumed_at == null && pauses_automation`. A red flag, an exhausted budget, a missing policy, an unknown wire outcome and the Govern route-to-human path all pause; an item that only owes a patient a reply does not.

project_id.description:
The project of the episode the hand-off was opened from. Null for a
hand-off opened without an episode, and for one about an application's
patient.

xuser_id.description: Null for Govern hand-offs; `application_id` and `patient_ref_hash` name the subject.

project_id.description: The project of the event's hand-off.

ChannelPolicy.description: A per-channel binding: the policy scope, the mode, and the consent requirement for one channel. An absent field means the channel's default.

project_id.description:
The project whose active policy decides this channel; `null` means the
application's own project. A policy belongs to one environment, so this
must be a live project of the organization in the application's
environment; any other is a `404`. Set from the console only: a request
made with a key may send back the value already stored, and may not
change it.

requires_consent.description: Whether an outbound turn on this channel requires a `granted` consent on record; absent means the channel's default (`sms`, `voice` and `email` require it).

ClaimMatch.description:
One term the gate matched in the evaluated text.

The evaluated text is the submitted content with leading and trailing
characters of the Unicode `White_Space` property removed (not the set
JavaScript's `trim` removes). Wherever a response carries that text, index
it rather than re-trimming. One entry per occurrence: a phrase that appears
twice is two matches with two ranges.

list.description: The vocabulary the entry belongs to.

phrase.description:
The policy entry that matched, as stored (lower-case). The matched
text itself is at `range`, and may differ in case, inflection,
hyphenation or apostrophe.

oneOf.description:
Where the match sits in the evaluated text. Present on every `term`
match; a client renders a message-level flag when it is absent.

reason.description: The policy author's reason for the entry; null when it has none.

ConsentRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/consent`. The reference travels in the body,
never in a path, so it is never in a request log.

at.description: When the patient granted or revoked; default now.

Counts.description:
Counts keyed by the raw gate decision (`allow`, `flag`,
`block_and_review`, `policy_missing`, `unavailable`; `rewrite` for turns
recorded before `flag` replaced it) for observe turns, and
by the binding answer (`allow`, `hold`, `block`) for enforce turns. An
observe `flag` (or `rewrite`) for a clinician audience is counted as
`flagged` instead: the clinician would have received the draft with its
matches.

CreateApplicationRequest.description:
A new application. It belongs to the request's project, which the body
does not name: the project selected in the console, or the key's own
project. That project's active policy, else the environment's default
policy, decides the application's turns.

oneOf.description: The per-patient message cap per fixed window; none by default.

The routing a hand-off opened for this application's patients is given:
queue label, primary and backup staff, response and
escalation seconds. Staff must be members of the organization.

red_flag_categories.description:
The red-flag categories the inbound screen runs with (`cardiac`,
`respiratory`, `neuro_stroke`, `self_harm`). Default: all four.

webhook_secret.description: The webhook signing secret, shown here once.

DecisionView.description:
The decision as the contract presents it, from `evaluate` and from the
poll. `released_content` and `deliverable_content` are the only fields that
can carry message text, and each does so under a stated condition.

decision_id.description: Absent only when the channel is `off`.

deliverable_content.description:
Clinician audience only, on a `flagged` decision: the draft as
evaluated, which is what to deliver. The service never rewrites a
draft, so this is your own content, trimmed. Never present for a
patient audience.

flagged.description:
The draft was delivered with flags: `allow` for a clinician audience
under a policy whose outcome is `flag`. Deliver the draft unchanged and
show the reader `matches`. `false` for a clean `allow` and for every
`hold` and `block`.

oneOf.description: The hand-off this decision opened or joined, with its current state.

inbound_flags.description: The red-flag rules the inbound matched; rule ids and categories only.

matches.description:
Each term behind a violation, positioned in the evaluated text. One
entry per occurrence, in reading order. Each carries the policy entry
(`phrase`), the list it belongs to, the policy author's `reason` (null
when the entry has none), how it was found (`source`; always `term`
today) and `range`, the span in UTF-16 code units with `end` exclusive.

The evaluated text is the `content` you sent with leading and trailing
characters of the Unicode `White_Space` property removed. That is not
what JavaScript's `String.prototype.trim` removes (it also removes
U+FEFF and keeps U+0085), so do not re-trim to find it: when
`deliverable_content` is present it is exactly the evaluated text, and
`deliverable_content.slice(range.start, range.end)` is the matched
text. Render a message-level flag for a match with no `range`. Empty on
decisions recorded before matches were.

model.description: The model the caller named for this turn, and its version. Null when the caller named none; never inferred.

oneOf.description:
What became of the reply: the outcome events on record, in the order
they were recorded, and the `state` they add up to (`delivered`, else
`superseded`, else `discarded`, else `failed`, else `released`). Null
until the first event. `superseded` is recorded by the service when a
later turn names this decision in `supersedes` or retries it.

released_content.description: Present once a reviewer released the held content: what to deliver.

retry_of.description: The decision this turn retries, when it is a retry. Null otherwise.

retryable.description:
Your application may write ONE new draft for this turn and evaluate
it with `retry_of` set to this `decision_id`.

`true` only when this turn was stopped in enforce mode, for a patient,
because of the draft's own content (the `reasons` name a clinical
claim the program may not make, or a missing disclaimer), the stop
class is `uncertain`, the policy does not review every send, and the
hold is still pending. It is `false` for a `never_sendable` stop, for
every stop about the patient rather than the draft (an opt-out, a
consent, a frequency cap, a missing disclosure), for a missing policy,
for a turn that is itself a retry at the platform's limit, for a turn
whose inbound routed the patient to a person, and once a reviewer has
acted. Add the `reasons` and the policy's rules to your
model's instructions; this service never writes the new draft.

review_url.description:
Console deep link for the customer's own reviewers, present when the
decision is in (or has been through) the review queue.

route_to_human.description:
A person must contact this patient. Independent of
`decision`: a clean draft can be `allow` with `route_to_human: true`,
and a violating one `hold` with it.

send_holding_line.description:
Send your holding line to this patient now.

This turn was stopped and the patient is waiting on a reply that is not coming, so the application sends the fixed text its clinical owner wrote: a person will reply, when, and what to do if it is urgent. **The contract says when, never what**: the text is the application's own, it is never model-written, and this service does not send it on the application's behalf.

`false` whenever another send would be the wrong thing rather than merely unnecessary: an opt-out, a missing or revoked consent, and a frequency cap each stop the turn because this patient should not be messaged, and a holding line is a message. It is also `false` in observe, where nothing was stopped and the caller was told to deliver.

One per stopped turn: each `evaluate` is one turn, so a second stopped draft in the same conversation is a second turn with its own answer.

show_hold_text.description:
Show your hold text in place of the stopped draft.

`true` when this turn was stopped (`hold` or `block` in enforce, not
released or rejected) and: the audience is `patient` and the channel is
in-session (`web_chat`, `app_message`, `voice`), where the patient is
waiting for the reply, whatever stopped the turn; or the audience is
`patient`, the channel is outbound (`sms`, `email`) and
`send_holding_line` is `true`; or the audience is `clinician`.

`false` on an outbound channel when no holding line is owed (send
nothing), on every `allow`, once a reviewer has released or rejected
the hold, once a retry of this turn or a turn that supersedes it has
been accepted (that turn's own field answers), and always in observe.
On a `retryable` turn, evaluate the retry first and show the hold text
only if the retry is stopped too. On an in-session channel the hold
text is the one reply: do not send a separate holding line there.

stop_class.description:
Which of the two stopped classes this turn is: `never_sendable` | `uncertain`, null when nothing was stopped.

In **enforce** it describes the `hold` the caller received: a never-sendable turn has no release path, so the application's own reviewers are told to record a replacement rather than wait for one. In **observe** it is read beside `would_have` and describes what the stop would have been: `would_have` keeps its documented vocabulary (the raw gate decision), and this carries the class the same turn was classified with.

superseded_by.description:
The decision that replaced this one: the turn that named it in
`supersedes`, or its retry. Null while nothing has replaced it. Read
from the `superseded` event in `outcome`.

supersedes.description:
The decisions this turn named in `supersedes` and replaced, in
ascending id order. Empty when it named none. The decision a retry
replaced is `retry_of`, not listed here.

turn_ref.description:
Your reference for the patient turn, as sent on `evaluate` (or, on a
retry sent without one, the reference of the decision it retries).
Null when none was sent.

webhook_deliveries.description:
The signed webhook deliveries about this decision: the
log, never the body.

would_have.description:
Observe: the raw gate decision (`allow` | `flag` | `block_and_review`
| `policy_missing`) or `unavailable`. Null in enforce. Decisions
recorded before `flag` replaced `rewrite` keep `rewrite`.

would_have_routed.description: Observe: the screen matched and would have routed; no task was opened.

established.description: The caller's own assertion; informational. The gate reads the ref.

ref.description:
The reference returned when THIS conversation's disclosure was
recorded. Any other value is ignored, and the turn is answered on
this conversation's own evidence, so a reference borrowed from
another conversation or application leaves the disclosure owed.

evidence_id.description: The evidence row; the id a reviewer sees in the console.

ref.description:
Attach this as `disclosure.ref` on every evaluate for the conversation.
`evaluate` also derives it from `conversation_id` when absent.

EvaluateRequest.description:
One turn to evaluate. A field this schema does not name is ignored, not
refused, so a misspelled `retry_of`, `turn_ref` or `supersedes` is a turn
that retries, groups and supersedes nothing.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

content.description: The draft the customer's AI produced.

oneOf.description:
The patient's message this turn answers. Screened by the
deterministic red-flag floor with the application's categories; a
match routes the patient to a person. Requires `patient_ref`.

metadata.description: Free JSON, stored and never evaluated.

oneOf.description:
Advisory. The application's configured mode decides; a hint that
disagrees is ignored.

model.description:
The model the caller's application ran for this turn, as the caller
names it. Recorded, never interpreted: the platform does
not run this model and has nothing to check the name against.

model_version.description:
That model's version, as the caller names it. Independent of `model`:
a caller that versions one and not the other is recorded as it is
rather than refused.

patient_ref.description: The customer's opaque patient identifier. Stored only as a SHA-256.

retry_of.description:
The decision this turn retries: a new draft written because that
decision came back `retryable`. It must name a decision of this
application and this conversation whose view says `retryable: true`,
and that has not been retried already; anything else is refused with
`400`, except `409` for a second retry of the same decision and for a
turn that was retryable until a reviewer released or rejected it, or
until another turn named it in `supersedes`. Two requests for one retry
under one `turn_id` record it once: the second is answered as a replay.
The new draft is judged exactly as any other turn. Send it with a NEW
`turn_id`. When the retry is `allow`, the hand-off the stopped turn
opened is resolved with the disposition `resolved_by_retry`, provided
that turn opened it, nothing else has joined it and nobody has claimed
it or acted on it.

supersedes.description:
The decisions this turn replaces, at most 8: earlier attempts at the
same patient turn that were never heard (a speculative reply the voice
platform discarded). Each must be a decision of this application and
this conversation, named once, and not the decision in `retry_of`
(`400` otherwise). An enforce decision still being decided, a decision
with a `delivered` event, one a reviewer released or rejected, or one
another turn already superseded is a `409`. In the same step as this
turn is recorded, each named decision leaves the review queue if it was
held, and its outcome records a `superseded` event naming this
decision. When this turn is `allow`, the hand-off a named stopped turn
opened is resolved with the disposition `resolved_by_supersession`
(`resolved_by_retry` when the turn in `retry_of` shares it), on the
conditions a retry's is; otherwise it stays open with a note naming
this decision. A replay of this `turn_id` returns the stored decision
and applies nothing again.

turn_id.description:
The idempotency key per application: a replay returns the stored
decision. Must not start with `govern:`, which is reserved for the
rows the platform writes.

turn_ref.description:
Your stable reference for the patient turn this draft answers: the
same value on every speculative re-send and retry of that turn, so the
attempts can be grouped. At most 128 printable characters. A retry
sent without one takes the reference of the decision it retries.
Stored as sent; never evaluated.

ExternalDecisionEvidence.description:
One Govern decision that opened or joined an external hand-off: the
evidence a person works from. `inbound_content` is the patient's own
message, PHI-visible on this staff-authorised surface only.

ExternalSubject.description: The subject of an external hand-off, for its readers.

patient_ref_hash.description: SHA-256 of the customer's opaque patient reference.

FrequencyCap.description:
The application's per-patient cap: at most `max_messages` per fixed window
of `window_seconds`, counted from the first message of the window.

remaining.description: Messages left in the current window (the full cap once it has lapsed).

GovernChannel.description: The channel vocabulary of the contract.

GovernMode.description:
Per policy, per application: is the gate consulted, and is its answer
binding? `Off` is not evaluated; `Observe` is evaluated and recorded as
`would_have` while the caller is always told allow; `Enforce` returns the
decision and it binds.

awaiting_reply.description: Which of these items carry a stopped draft nobody has answered yet. A patient has one open item, so a stop joins whatever they already have (a paused automation, a flagged inbound). The item keeps the reason it was opened for, and this lists what it now also owes.

HandoffRef.description: The hand-off a decision opened or joined, as the contract shows it.

pauses_automation.description:
Whether this hand-off also pauses automated messaging to the subject.
`automation_resumed_at == null` says a person owns it;
this says whether the application should stop sending meanwhile. The
two are read together: still paused is
`automation_resumed_at == null && pauses_automation`.

InboundFlag.description:
One red-flag rule the inbound matched. Rule id and category only; never
the text.

InboundMessage.description: The patient's message this turn answers.

MatchList.description: Which vocabulary a match came from.

MatchRange.description:
Where a match sits in the evaluated text, in UTF-16 code units (the unit
of JavaScript string indices). `start` is inclusive and `end` exclusive, so
`text.slice(start, end)` is the matched span.

secret.description: The raw key. This is its only appearance; store it server-side.

MintedKeyDto.description: A key at mint time: the metadata plus the secret, which is shown once.

MintedWebhookSecret.description: A freshly minted signing secret: the plaintext, shown once, and when.

webhook_secret.description: The secret. This is its only appearance; store it server-side.

webhook_secret_hint.description: Its last four characters, for telling secrets apart.

ModelBreakdown.description: The same counts, per model and version the caller named. A bucket with both fields null counts the turns whose caller named no model. Send a stable model name so the report stays readable.

OptOutRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/opt-out`. `opted_out: false` records the
patient opting back in, which the application may do only for an opt-out
it recorded itself.

OutcomeEvent.description: One event in a decision's outcome trail.

at.description: When it happened, as the writer said.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the text; on `released` and `delivered` only.

hash_matches_release.description:
Whether `content_hash` matches the content the record says was
deliverable. `null` with no hash, or when there was nothing to compare
against. Computed when the event is recorded; a later release does not
change it.

superseded_by.description: The decision that replaced this one; on `superseded` only.

OutcomeKind.description:
What happened to a decision's reply: the kind of an event, and, for the
trail as a whole, its derived `state`.

content_hash.description:
SHA-256, hex, of the UTF-8 text released or delivered. Required for
`released` and `delivered`; refused on any other kind.

delivery_ref.description: Your own reference for the delivery (a message id, a row id).

kind.description:
`released`, `delivered`, `discarded` or `failed`. `superseded` is
reserved for the service and refused here.

reason.description:
A short reason code, for example why a reply was discarded or why an
attempt failed. Never message text.

OutcomeView.description:
A decision's outcome: the state its events add up to, and the events in
the order they were recorded.

state.description:
The kind that decides where the outcome stands, derived from the
events and never stored: `delivered` if a delivered event exists, else
`superseded`, else `discarded`, else `failed`, else `released`.

PatchApplicationRequest.description:
Every field optional; only the ones present change. `channel_policies`
replaces the whole map when present (send the full map back).

oneOf.description: `null` removes the cap; omit to leave it unchanged.

`null` clears the routing; hand-offs then open with the
organization's default queue and no deadlines.

red_flag_categories.description: Replaces the whole list when present; must not be empty.

PatientStateRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/state`: a read, as a POST so the reference
stays out of the URL.

PatientStateView.description: The state as the contract shows it. The reference itself is never in it.

events.description: The most recent transitions, newest first (at most twenty).

Rates.description:
Fractions in `[0, 1]`, never percentages. Each is `null` when its
denominator is zero.

enforced_held.description:
The share of answered enforce turns whose answer was not `allow`, over
`totals.answered_enforce`. Turns the gate did not answer are on
neither side of it.

unanswered.description:
The share of every record in the window that the gate did not answer:
`totals.unavailable` over `totals.decisions`.

would_have_flagged.description:
The share of answered observe turns that would have been delivered
with flags: a `flag` for a clinician audience, over
`totals.answered_observe`.

would_have_withheld.description:
The share of answered observe turns whose would-have answer was not
`allow`, over `totals.answered_observe`. Turns the gate did not answer
are on neither side of it. A `flag` for a clinician audience is not
withheld (the clinician receives the draft with its matches) and is
counted in `would_have_flagged` instead; a `flag` for a patient is
withheld.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

text_shown.description: The disclosure text the patient was shown, verbatim.

overlap_seconds.description:
How long the previous keys keep authenticating after this rotation.
Default one day; at most seven. Zero refuses the previous keys at once.

previous_keys_expire_at.description: When every previous key of the application stops authenticating.

escalation_seconds.description: Additional elapsed time after the response deadline before backup routing.

StopClassBreakdown.description:
The same counts, per stop class: `never_sendable` or `uncertain` for the
turns that were stopped (in observe, that would have been stopped), and a
bucket with a null class for the turns that were not, or not yet answered.

answered_enforce.description:
Enforce records the gate answered: neither pending nor unavailable.
The denominator of `rates.enforced_held`.

answered_observe.description:
Observe records the gate answered: neither pending nor unavailable.
The denominator of `rates.would_have_withheld`.

decisions.description: Every decision record in the window, any mode or status.

transcript.description:
Records that came from a transcript batch rather than a
live call; always observe, counted in `observe` as well.

unavailable.description:
Records the gate did not answer, in either mode. The caller received
its mode's fallback; these records are in neither rate.

would_have_flagged.description:
Answered observe records that would have been delivered to a
clinician with flags: the numerator of `rates.would_have_flagged`.

would_have_withheld.description:
Answered observe records whose would-have answer withheld the draft:
the numerator of `rates.would_have_withheld`.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

turns.description: One to 1,000 turns; `turn_id` unique within the batch.

TranscriptJobView.description: A job as the contract presents it. Counts, never text.

abandoned.description:
Turns a failed job gave up on: never evaluated, no decision, their
text cleared with the job. Only ever non-zero when `status` is
`failed`.

unavailable.description: Evaluated turns the gate did not answer for.

would_have.description:
Raw gate decisions over the evaluated turns that are decided:
`allow`, `flag` (`rewrite` before it replaced it), `block_and_review`, `policy_missing`,
`unavailable`.

TranscriptTurn.description: One past turn as the customer posts it.

model.description: The model that produced the turn, and its version, as the caller names them. Optional; recorded on the decision, never interpreted. Batches from before and after a model change are told apart by these.

sent_at.description: When it went out. The observe report windows on it.

turn_id.description:
The idempotency key per application: a turn the application already
has a decision for is a `duplicate`. Must not start with `govern:`,
which is reserved for the rows the platform writes.

TranscriptTurnView.description: One turn of a job, with the decision it produced or matched.

oneOf.description: Absent until the turn is processed.

WebhookDeliveryView.description:
A delivery as the contract shows it on the decision. Counts and codes,
never the body.

subject_version.description:
The revision of the subject this delivery is about: the hand-off's
`version` at the change, or `0` for an event keyed to the subject's
whole lifetime. Two deliveries of one event differ here.
